issues.legal_issue: An appellate court reversing a trial court’s decision must decide the trial court’s finding that the suit is barred by limitation before reversing the judgment.
material_facts: Limitation was pleaded in the written statement, although no specific issue on limitation was framed.
The trial court found that the suit was barred by limitation.
The first appellate court reversed the trial court’s judgment without deciding the limitation issue, and the High Court affirmed that decision without addressing it.
issues.conclusion: The first appellate court and the High Court could not reverse the trial court’s judgment while leaving its finding that the suit was barred by limitation undecided. Their judgments were set aside, and the suit was remanded to the first appellate court to decide that limited question.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(1) of the Limitation Act, 1963, requires a court to dismiss a suit, appeal or application brought after the prescribed period even if limitation has not been pleaded as a defence. Order 7 Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure also requires rejection of a plaint where it appears from the plaint that the suit is barred by law. A trial court’s limitation finding must therefore be addressed before an appellate court reverses the judgment. The Court noted that State of Punjab v. Darshan Singh did not appear to have considered Section 3(1).

predicates.appeal_reverses_trial_judgment: The proceeding is an appeal in which a court is asked to reverse a trial court’s judgment.
predicates.trial_found_suit_time_barred: The trial court found that the suit was filed after the applicable limitation period.
predicates.appellate_left_limitation_finding_unreso: The appellate court did not decide or set aside the trial court’s finding on limitation.

issues.definition: If an appeal seeks reversal of a trial judgment, the trial court found the suit time-barred, and the appellate court left that finding unresolved, the appellate court must decide limitation before reversing.

issues.legal_issue: A limitation issue may be considered at the final appellate stage when it was pleaded and decided at trial, even if it was not raised before the intermediate appellate courts and involves a mixed question of law and fact.
material_facts: The limitation defence was pleaded in the written statement and, despite the absence of a specific issue, the trial court decided that the suit was barred by limitation.
The first appellate court reversed the trial court’s decision without setting aside its limitation finding, and the High Court affirmed that decision without addressing the finding.
The limitation point was not raised before the first appellate court or the High Court, and it was raised in the appeal before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The limitation point could be considered in the appeal before the Supreme Court because it had been pleaded and decided at trial and the trial court’s finding had not been set aside by the appellate courts.
issues.legal_principle: Although Balasaria Construction (P) Ltd. v. Hanuman Seva Trust and Narne Rama Murthy v. Ravula Somasundram recognize that a limitation issue involving mixed questions of law and fact generally cannot be raised for the first time at the appellate stage, that proposition did not prevent consideration here: the defence had been pleaded and decided at trial. The Court relied on Lachhmi Sewak Sahu v. Ram Rup Sahu for the principle that a limitation point is prima facie admissible even in the court of last resort, though not taken in the lower courts. It also observed that limitation may concern the court’s jurisdiction and that Section 3(1) of the Limitation Act, 1963, imposes a duty to address it.

rule.if: final_appellate_review and limitation_defense_pleaded_at_trial and trial_decided_limitation and trial_finding_not_set_aside_on_appeal

predicates.final_appellate_review: The proceeding is a final appeal challenging the outcome of lower-court proceedings.
predicates.limitation_defense_pleaded_at_trial: A party raised limitation as a defence in the trial court.
predicates.trial_decided_limitation: The trial court made a decision on whether the suit was time-barred.
predicates.trial_finding_not_set_aside_on_appeal: The appellate courts did not set aside the trial court’s decision on limitation.

issues.definition: If final appellate review follows a limitation defence pleaded and decided at trial, and the trial court’s limitation finding was not set aside on appeal, the limitation issue may be considered at the final appellate stage.
